question: Should OpenClaw sponsor this experimental core grouped-Claw lifecycle and consent-planning layer as an ordered stack, rather than keep the capability outside the core runtime for now?
rationale: The patch adds a broad core CLI, state-ownership, capability-consent, and future update-execution foundation; implementation quality alone cannot determine whether that permanent product boundary should be accepted.

options.title: Sponsor the staged core design
options.body: Keep the planner as a separately gated foundation, require exact-head redaction proof, and land it only in dependency order after its parent slices.

options.title: Narrow the core boundary
options.body: Retain only generic lifecycle primitives in core and move higher-level grouped update policy to an extension surface before reconsidering this PR.

options.title: Pause the RFC stack
options.body: Defer the experimental Claw lifecycle direction until a maintainer confirms the supported product and upgrade model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the staged core design
recommendation.body: Keep the planner as a separately gated foundation, require exact-head redaction proof, and land it only in dependency order after its parent slices.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is assigned to this PR and has already set the most specific review constraints for its planning and ownership boundary.
